title: Elephant vs Blue Whale vs Pando | Heaviest Living Things Comparison #shorts
description_hook: From a 10.9-tonne record elephant to a 5,900-tonne aspen, Earth's heaviest living things ranked by weight, plus one nobody can weigh.

items.name: RECORD ELEPHANT
items.label: 10.9 T
items.say: What's the heaviest living thing on Earth, by weight? Start with the record elephant: about 10.9 tonnes.
items.img: a massive African savanna bull elephant with long curved tusks standing on dry golden grassland at sunset, dust in the air, low angle

items.name: BLUE WHALE
items.label: 150 T
items.say: An Antarctic blue whale. Up to 150 tonnes.
items.img: an enormous blue whale gliding through clear sunlit ocean water seen from below, light rays across its long mottled back

items.name: GENERAL SHERMAN TREE
items.label: 1,270 T
items.say: General Sherman, the biggest tree by volume. Its trunk alone weighs nearly 1,400 tons. About 1,270 tonnes.
items.img: a colossal giant sequoia trunk with thick red furrowed bark rising out of a misty mountain forest, tiny hiker silhouette at its base for scale

items.name: PANDO ASPEN
items.label: 5,900 T
items.say: Pando. Looks like a forest of more than 47,000 trunks. It's one aspen in Utah. An estimated 5,900 tonnes.
items.img: a vast grove of identical white-barked aspen trees with glowing yellow autumn leaves covering a rolling hillside, aerial view

items.name: HONEY FUNGUS
items.say: But one honey fungus in Oregon spreads underground across about 965 hectares. More than 20 times Pando's area. Nobody can weigh it.
items.img: clusters of honey-colored mushrooms on a mossy conifer forest floor with dark root-like strands spreading through the soil below, cross-section view

gumi.say: A tree that's a forest, and a fungus too big to weigh. Which one surprised you?
